nodes.content: Develop a learned turbulence closure that captures bidirectional energy transfer and remains stable across unseen coarse-graining scales.
requirements: Achieve below 10% energy-spectrum error against filtered direct numerical simulations at two unseen filter widths.
Maintain bounded kinetic energy and correct mean subgrid dissipation while reproducing intermittent backscatter.

nodes.content: Train a log-filter-width-conditioned equivariant closure combining mean-dissipation-calibrated eddy viscosity with energy-budget-capped stochastic backscatter.
How should the backscatter energy cap scale with filter width to preserve extreme transfer events without destabilizing coarse-grid integration?
Δ²|S|³-scaled backscatter caps achieve ≥90% DNS top-decile event recall while keeping kinetic energy within 20% of DNS at unseen widths.
Fit on isotropic DNS at Δ=8η,12η; compare strain-scaled and fixed caps at held-out 10η,16η for backscatter recall and energy drift.
Run a posteriori LES at 10η and 16η comparing Δ²|S|³ versus fixed caps; measure top-decile backscatter recall and kinetic-energy drift.
At 10η/16η, strain-scaled recall was 74%/63% versus fixed-cap 69%/57%, missing 90% despite <12% energy drift.
A vorticity-alignment multiplier on Δ²|S|³, constrained by global energy budget, yields ≥80% backscatter recall and <15% energy drift at 16η.
Ablate the vorticity-alignment multiplier in held-out 10η/16η LES; measure top-decile backscatter recall, kinetic-energy drift, and mean subgrid dissipation.
At 10η/16η, alignment raised recall to 88%/82% (from 74%/63%), with 8%/11% energy drift and mean dissipation within 5% of DNS.
Replace recall-deficient strain-only caps with vorticity-aligned caps: held-out recall reaches ≥82% with ≤11% energy drift.
Benchmark adopted alignment against strain-only and fixed caps at 10η/16η; report backscatter recall, energy drift, and spectrum error.
Held-out LES benchmark report tabulates 10η/16η spectrum error, backscatter recall, and kinetic-energy drift for aligned, strain-only, and fixed caps.
Does vorticity alignment achieve <10% spectrum error at both unseen widths without sacrificing energy stability or backscatter recall?
Use filter-width-conditioned differentiable deconvolution to reconstruct signed stresses, paired with Germano-calibrated viscosity and global kinetic-energy control.
Train deconvolution on 8η/12η DNS; benchmark 10η/16η LES against aligned caps for spectrum error, energy bounds, mean dissipation, and backscatter.
Using the benchmark report’s matched 10η/16η protocol, run deconvolution LES and compare spectra, energy drift, dissipation, and backscatter recall.
Matched-width LES comparison table records deconvolution versus aligned-cap spectrum error, energy drift, mean dissipation, and backscatter recall at 10η/16η.
Audit the matched-width LES table, comparing both closures’ 10η/16η spectrum errors against 10%, alongside energy drift, dissipation, and backscatter recall.
At 10η/16η, deconvolution yielded 7%/8% spectrum error versus aligned-cap 11%/14%, ≤12% energy drift, ≤5% dissipation bias, ≥82% backscatter recall.
Stress-test deconvolution under 20% higher forcing at 10η/16η; check energy bounds, spectrum error, dissipation bias, and backscatter recall.
Under 20% stronger forcing, deconvolution’s 16η spectrum error rose to 19%, energy drift to 28%, dissipation bias to 22%.
Retain deconvolution for nominal forcing, but defer deployment until adaptive dissipation corrects 16η high-forcing energy drift and spectrum error.
Blend deconvolution stresses with vorticity-aligned capped backscatter using a forcing-aware gate and enforce a discrete kinetic-energy inequality.
What forcing-normalized energy-budget threshold should activate aligned-cap blending at 16η without suppressing top-decile backscatter?
Gate blending when domain-integrated backscatter exceeds 15% of running-mean forcing power; expect ≤15% energy drift and ≥80% recall at 16η.
Sweep 10%–20% gate thresholds in 10η/16η high-forcing LES; measure energy drift, backscatter recall, and spectrum error.
At 16η under 20% stronger forcing, the 15% gate held energy drift to 13% but backscatter recall fell to 72%.
Raise the gate to 20% of mean forcing power with selective eddy-viscosity compensation; predict ≤15% drift, ≥80% recall at 16η.
Run 10η/16η LES under 20% stronger forcing with 20% gate and selective viscosity; measure energy drift, top-decile recall, spectrum error.
Under 20% stronger forcing, the 20% gate yielded 10η/16η spectrum errors 7%/9%, energy drift 9%/14%, recall 86%/81%, dissipation bias 4%/6%.
Train a scale-equivariant wavelet flux network with signed interband transfers and mean-calibrated, budget-projected dissipation.
Train on 8η/12η DNS; benchmark 10η/16η LES against gated blending under nominal and 20%-stronger forcing for spectra, stability, dissipation, backscatter.
Train the wavelet flux network on 8η/12η DNS and run 10η/16η LES under nominal and 20%-stronger forcing.
WaveletFlux-v1 checkpoint and matched LES logs contain 10η/16η spectra, kinetic-energy traces, dissipation rates, and signed-transfer events for both forcings.
Compare WaveletFlux-v1 logs against gated blending at 10η/16η under both forcings: spectrum error, energy drift, dissipation bias, backscatter recall.
At 16η under stronger forcing, WaveletFlux-v1 had 16% spectrum error versus gated blending’s 9%, despite 12% energy drift.
Couple scale-conditioned neural stress to a nonnegative subgrid-energy reservoir; fund backscatter from stored energy and calibrate mean dissipation.
Which filter-width-dependent reservoir turnover time preserves 16η high-forcing backscatter bursts without biasing mean subgrid dissipation?
A reservoir turnover time τ=0.6Δ/√k_sgs yields ≥80% backscatter recall, ≤5% dissipation bias, and ≤15% energy drift at high-forcing 16η.
Run 16η LES under 20%-stronger forcing with τ coefficients 0.3, 0.6, 1.0; measure backscatter recall, dissipation bias, energy drift.
At high-forcing 16η, τ=0.6Δ/√k_sgs achieved 84% recall, 4% dissipation bias, and 11% energy drift.
Benchmark reservoir, gated blending, and deconvolution at 10η/16η under both forcings; compare spectrum error, energy drift, dissipation bias, backscatter recall.
At high-forcing 16η, deconvolution/gated/reservoir spectrum errors were 19%/9%/8% and energy drifts 28%/14%/11%; gated/reservoir backscatter recall reached 81%/84%.
Does the reservoir’s 16η advantage persist at 10η and nominal forcing, or does limited stored energy suppress backscatter?
At nominal forcing, the reservoir achieves <10% spectrum error and ≥80% backscatter recall at 10η/16η, with <5% reservoir-empty cells.
Compare reservoir and gated blending in nominal 10η/16η LES; measure spectrum error, backscatter recall, reservoir-empty fraction, and energy drift.
Nominal 10η/16η: reservoir spectrum error 7%/8%, recall 86%/82%, empty cells 3%/4%; gated blending error 11%/12%.
Advance the reservoir closure to independent-seed validation at 10η/16η under both forcings; check spectra, energy bounds, dissipation, backscatter.
Run three independent-seed reservoir LES at 10η/16η under both forcings; compare DNS spectra, energy bounds, mean dissipation, and backscatter recall.
Three-seed 10η/16η LES: spectrum error 7–9% under both forcings, energy drift ≤13%, dissipation bias ≤5%, backscatter recall ≥81%.
Select reservoir over gated blending and deconvolution: three-seed spectrum error ≤9%, energy drift ≤13%, dissipation bias ≤5%, recall ≥81%.
Using the selected reservoir and benchmark report, run long-horizon 10η/16η LES assessing spectrum error, energy bounds, dissipation, and backscatter.
Reservoir long-horizon validation package contains 10η/16η LES trajectories, filtered-DNS spectra, kinetic-energy bounds, dissipation statistics, and backscatter-event counts.
